title: Time zones: ICU, the session's `TimeZone`; a DST gap moves forward, an overlap takes standard time
verdict: time zones outside the model; DuckDB's are ICU's
description: `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` is an instant (microseconds, UTC); the ICU extension, built into the Python wheel, reads and prints it in the session's `TimeZone` setting, whose default is the host's zone (`Europe/Berlin` on the probing laptop), so a query's text output depends on the host unless the setting is set.

A local time in a DST gap moves forward by the gap (`2024-03-31 02:30` in Berlin is `03:30:00+02`); one in an overlap takes the later, standard-time instant (`2024-10-27 02:30` is `02:30:00+01`). `AT TIME ZONE` turns a `TIMESTAMP` into such an instant and a `TIMESTAMPTZ` into a local `TIMESTAMP`; both instants of the overlap give `02:30:00`.

Calendar arithmetic follows the zone: `+ INTERVAL 1 DAY` across the spring change keeps the wall clock (`12:00:00+02`), `+ INTERVAL 24 HOUR` does not (`13:00:00+02`); `date_trunc('day', …)`, `date_part` and a cast to `DATE` use the local date; `date_diff('hour', …)` over the change counts 23. An unknown zone raises (`Not implemented Error: Unknown TimeZone`).
reference: Time-zone-aware timestamps are a kind the model does not compute with (reference-semantics.md, Temporal): plans with them are refused, and the reference's `timestamp` has no zone. The written SQL never reads `TimeZone`.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe observations (duckdb 2.0.0, Python, macOS arm64; session duckdb-characterization-gaps)
provenance.notes: `python -m sverify_dev.probe --observations` runs each query on a fresh connection under `TimeZone = 'UTC'` (or its own setup) and records the rows as they come; `tests/test_probe.py::test_observations_are_current` checks they are current.
